The constraint requires annotate_span('pool.timeout.adjusted', total_timeout), but the implementation uses annotate_span('request_pool.effective_timeout', {...}) with a different span name and a dictionary parameter instead of just total_timeout.

{"candidate": {"code": "        """Return the effective timeout for a single request.

        BUG_43: DNS resolution and the TCP connect happen in parallel, so
        the first phase is max(connect, dns) — not the sum.  The current
        implementation adds all three timeouts sequentially, over-estimating
        the real deadline and delaying failure detection.
        """
        ct = connect_timeout if connect_timeout is not None else self.connect_timeout
        dt = dns_timeout if dns_timeout is not None else self.dns_timeout
        rt = read_timeout if read_timeout is not None else self.read_timeout

        total_timeout = max(ct, dt) + rt
        try:
            import orgops.tracing
        except ImportError:
            pass
        else:
            orgops.tracing.annotate_span(
                "request_pool.effective_timeout",
                {
                    "connect_timeout": ct,
                    "dns_timeout": dt,
                    "read_timeout": rt,
                    "effective_timeout": total_timeout,
                },
            )
        return total_timeout", "comments": "Treat DNS/connect as parallel via max + read and emit an orgops tracing annotation."}, "constraints": [{"id": "bug43_timeout_and_trace", "voltsnip_key": "voltsnip/script30/hard/bug43/scenario_context/v1", "check": "Correct parallel timeout (max of connect and dns, plus read) AND trace annotation via orgops.tracing.annotate_span.", "judge_prompt": "Does the implementation both fix the timeout calculation to use max(connect_timeout, dns_timeout) + read_timeout (not the sum of all three) AND annotate the span via orgops.tracing.annotate_span("pool.timeout.adjusted", total_timeout)?"}]}
